correctness.rationale: For every nonnegative tolerance, the centered pair-sum identity bounds each coordinate by three halves of that tolerance on the event. Each coordinate of the symmetric construction is uniform on an interval of length three because six disjoint half-unit affine images carry equal weights. Each pair sum lies between minus one and one. Scaling into the central interval and mixing with exact complement-uniform distributions restores the standard-uniform marginals and attains the three-times-tolerance probability below the one-third threshold. The zero and saturation endpoints are treated separately. The rational checker is supplemental to the proof.

value.rationale: Simultaneous perfect antitheticity of three continuous uniform marginals is impossible despite individual bivariate feasibility. A complete sharp tolerance-to-probability law, exact critical compatibility threshold 1/3 and explicit measure-preserving extremizer resolve this natural multivariate negative-dependence capacity question. The law is not a fixed sample enumeration or arbitrary narrow parameter choice.
